43008729.titulo: Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90 supports DNA replication
43008729.autores: Ibrasheva G, Chen Y, … Derbyshire ER (6 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: A chaperona PfHsp90 de Plasmodium falciparum é um alvo antimalárico validado, mas faltava mapear quais complexos moleculares dependem diretamente de sua atividade nos estágios sanguíneo e hepático.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Proteômica quantitativa no estágio sanguíneo sob dois inibidores químicos distintos de Hsp90 (geldanamicina e XL888), co-imunoprecipitação (Co-IP) de clientes e ensaios de síntese nascente de DNA em fases eritrocítica e hepática.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Identificadas 131 proteínas depletadas por ambos os inibidores (40% co-imunoprecipitadas com PfHsp90), com forte enriquecimento em replicação de DNA; inibir PfHsp90 reduziu conteúdo de DNA, bloqueou síntese nascente e gerou sinergismo com inibidores de replicação.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Abre estratégia sinérgica para bloquear proliferação de Plasmodium combinando moduladores de proteostase (PfHsp90) e estresse replicativo em modelos celulares e murinos do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Testar se a inibição subletal de Hsp90 potencializa danos oxidativos ao DNA parasitário induzidos por hemo livre e estresse redox eritrocitário.

43008729.resumo: Plasmodium falciparum heat shock protein 90 (PfHsp90) is an attractive antimalarial target, but the molecular pathways dependent on its activity remain poorly understood. Here, we use two chemically distinct Hsp90 inhibitors, geldanamycin and XL888, to profile the PfHsp90-dependent proteome during the blood stage. We identify 131 proteins reduced in abundance following both treatments, 40% of which co-immunoprecipitate with PfHsp90. DNA replication emerges as the most enriched pathway, and PfHsp90 inhibition reduces parasite DNA content and nascent DNA synthesis during blood- and liver-stage development. Combining Hsp90 inhibition with inhibitors of DNA replication further produces synergistic antiparasitic activity. Together, these findings establish a functional connection between PfHsp90 and parasite DNA replication and define a network of conserved and Plasmodium-specific proteins dependent on Hsp90 activity.

43015796.titulo: Role of Anopheles funestus in sustaining residual malaria transmission in central Senegal
43015796.autores: Faye MB, Dia AK, … Samb B (12 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Em regiões endêmicas africanas, Anopheles funestus frequentemente substitui An. gambiae s.l. durante a estação seca, sustentando a transmissão residual de Plasmodium falciparum.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Coleta de 6.932 anofelinos em dois distritos do Senegal central por captura em isca humana (HLC) e borrifação intradomiciliar (PSC), identificação por chave dicotômica + PCR específica de grupo e ELISA para proteína circunsporozoíta (CSP) e fonte de repasto sanguíneo.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Anopheles funestus s.s. correspondeu a 73,7% (5.108/6.932) da fauna coletada, com taxa de esporozoítos de 0,3% e taxa de inoculação entomológica (EIR) de 0,008 a 0,038 picadas infectantes por pessoa/noite, sustentando a transmissão contínua.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Reforça parâmetros reais de competência vetorial e densidade intradomiciliar em estudos comparativos de anofelinos e transmissão residual.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Comparar curvas de sobrevivência pós-repasto e suscetibilidade a Plasmodium entre linhagens mantidas no insetário sob sazonalidade nutricional simulada.

43015796.resumo:
Anopheles funestus is one of the major malaria vectors in sub-Saharan Africa. In Senegal, it is found across nearly all biogeographical areas, often replacing An. gambiae s.l. and sustaining malaria transmission during the dry season. Despite its recognized role as a major vector, the specific contribution of An. funestus to malaria transmission in many malaria-endemic areas remains underexplored. This study aims to assess the contribution of An. funestus in malaria transmission in two health districts in Central Senegal.
Adult mosquitoes were collected from July 2018 to November 2019 in the health districts of Nioro (Ndramé Ndimb) and Ndoffane (Tawa Mboudaye) using Human Landing Catches (HLCs) and Pyrethrum Spray Catches (PSCs). Anopheline specimens were identified morphologically using standard dichotomous keys, with species confirmation performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Plasmodium falciparum infection and blood meals sources were determined using Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) techniques.
A total of 6,932 Anopheles mosquitoes were collected. Of these, 73.7% (5,108/6,932) were identified as An. funestus, which was the predominant species at both study sites, with 1,364 specimens collected in Nioro and 3,744 in Ndoffane. Molecular analysis confirmed that An. funestus sensu stricto (s.s) was the only member of the An. funestus group recorded. In Ndramé Ndimb, the mean human biting rate and indoor resting density were 2.8 bites per person per night (b/p/n) and 9.0 females per room (f/r), respectively, compared to 12.4 b/p/n and 19.1 f/r in Tawa Mboudaye. The P. falciparum circumsporozoite rate was 0.3% in both villages, resulting in estimated entomological inoculation rates (EIRs) of 0.008 and 0.038 infected bites per person per night in Ndramé Ndimb and Tawa Mboudaye, respectively. The human blood index was relatively low, with only 22.3% (324/1,452) of An. funestus specimens found to have fed on humans.
This study highlights the predominance of An. funestus and its important role in sustaining residual malaria transmission in central Senegal, even where overall transmission intensity remains low.

43015880.titulo: Optimizing bacterial enrichment procedures to improve mosquito midgut microbiome research
43015880.autores: Schrieke H, Trouche B, … Reveillaud J (5 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: O microbioma do intestino médio de Aedes aegypti governa desenvolvimento, ovogênese e competência vetorial, mas o excesso de DNA eucariótico do hospedeiro satura bibliotecas metagenômicas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Comparação sistemática de três protocolos de extração em pools de intestinos médios de Aedes aegypti — DNeasy Blood & Tissue com/sem filtração em 5 μm e QIAamp Microbiome (lise diferencial + depleção enzimática de DNA do hospedeiro) — com qPCR, perfil taxonômico SSU rRNA e reconstrução de MAGs.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O kit QIAamp Microbiome alcançou o maior enriquecimento bacteriano e reconstrução de MAGs preservando >85% dos táxons (com maior recuperação de Gammaproteobacteria sem perda de diversidade global), enquanto os métodos DNeasy recuperaram maior amplitude de filos raros e NTUs exclusivas.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Define o protocolo padrão para o LUCHM caracterizar o impacto da dieta HFHS na microbiota comensal intestinal de Aedes aegypti sem mascaramento por DNA do mosquito.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Combinar depleção diferencial (Microbiome kit) com extração total em fêmeas pós-repasto HFHS para capturar alterações em Enterococcus e Gammaproteobacteria produtoras de metabólitos.

43015880.resumo: Mosquitoes are major vectors of infectious diseases, with their midgut microbiota playing a crucial role in host development, reproduction, and pathogen interactions. However, characterizing midgut microbial communities remains challenging because host DNA often dominates metagenomic libraries, reducing the resolution of bacterial community profiling and hindering the recovery of microbial genomes. To evaluate strategies for bacterial DNA enrichment in this context, we compared three DNA extraction protocols applied to pooled Aedes aegypti midguts: (i) the QIAGEN DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit without filtration (DNeasy NF), (ii) the same kit preceded by a 5 μm filtration step to reduce eukaryotic material (DNeasy F), and (iii) the QIAGEN QIAamp Microbiome kit, which combines differential host cell lysis and enzymatic DNA depletion. Each method was assessed using qPCR-based quantification of bacterial and host DNA, SSU rRNA-based taxonomic profiling of metagenomic reads, and Metagenome-Assembled Genomes (MAGs) reconstruction using advanced binning approaches. Our results show that while the Microbiome kit provided the highest bacterial enrichment and captured a large fraction (> 85%) of the bacterial taxa detected with the other kits, it yielded a higher relative abundance of Gammaproteobacteria. This occurred without a loss of overall diversity, suggesting improved recovery of microbial taxa rather than a compositional bias. The filtration step associated with the DNeasy kit significantly reduced host DNA but also lowered bacterial material, allowing MAG reconstruction, though less efficiently than the Microbiome kit. Despite this, the DNeasy methods allowed recovering a broader range of bacterial phyla with a more even distribution across taxa, while each extraction method also detected a unique set of NTUs. Overall, a combination of DNA extraction methods may be necessary to optimize microbiome analysis in mosquito midguts, facilitating a more comprehensive understanding of microbial diversity and its potential applications in vector control strategies.

43015880.implicacao: Define o protocolo padrão para o LUCHM caracterizar o impacto da dieta HFHS na microbiota comensal intestinal de Aedes aegypti sem mascaramento por DNA do mosquito.

43017112.titulo: Individual variation in food odor sensitivity is related to neuropeptide signaling and starvation in
43017112.autores: Okumura M, Shibukawa Y, … Chihara T (6 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Mesmo dentro de estoques geneticamente homogêneos de dípteros, existe ampla variação individual na sensibilidade olfatória a odores alimentares.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Classificação comportamental sequencial em armadilhas olfatórias de Drosophila isogênica seguida de transcriptômica comparativa (RNA-seq), quantificação de triacilgliceróis e ensaios de jejum/realimentação.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Moscas hipersensíveis ao odor apresentaram reservas reduzidas de triacilgliceróis, maior suscetibilidade ao jejum e expressão elevada do receptor neuropeptídico sNPF-R; a alimentação reverteu o fenótipo de atração olfatória.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta diretamente estoques lipídicos (triacilgliceróis em gotículas lipídicas) e sinalização neuropeptídica tipo sNPF/CCHa2 ao comportamento alimentar pós-dieta em insetos.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Neurobiologia, Neuropeptídeos & Eixo Intestino-Cérebro' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Investigar se fêmeas de Aedes alimentadas com dieta HFHS apresentam dessensibilização prolongada de busca hospedeira mediada por sNPF-R e acúmulo de TAG.

43017112.resumo: Olfaction is fundamental for animal survival, and individual variation exists in olfactory sensitivity. However, the underlying mechanisms of such variations remain unclear. We classified Drosophila with different olfactory sensitivities toward food-related odors from the same genetic stock using sequential olfactory trap assays. Transcriptome analysis of sensitive and insensitive flies, defined by consistent attraction or non-attraction across three assays, revealed differential expression of genes associated with chemosensation, lipid metabolism, and lipid transport. Flies attracted to food-related odors exhibited lower triacylglycerol levels than non-attracted flies. Sensitive flies also expressed higher levels of sNPF-R, a neuropeptide receptor induced by starvation, despite all flies being exposed to the same starvation stress before the trap assays. Moreover, sensitive flies were more vulnerable to starvation, and feeding decreased their attraction to food-related odors. Together, these findings indicate that individual variation in internal physiological state, particularly starvation level, influences olfactory sensitivity to food-related odors through neuropeptide signaling.
43017112.metodo: Classificação comportamental sequencial em armadilhas olfatórias de Drosophila isogênica seguida de transcriptômica comparativa (RNA-seq), quantificação de triacilgliceróis e ensaios de jejum/realimentação.
43017112.implicacao: Conecta diretamente estoques lipídicos (triacilgliceróis em gotículas lipídicas) e sinalização neuropeptídica tipo sNPF/CCHa2 ao comportamento alimentar pós-dieta em insetos.
43017112.faisca_lateral: 💡 Investigar se fêmeas de Aedes alimentadas com dieta HFHS apresentam dessensibilização prolongada de busca hospedeira mediada por sNPF-R e acúmulo de TAG.

43015033.titulo: Mosquito vector abundance, spatial distribution and arboviral transmission risk in high-traffic cross-border zones of Tanzania
43015033.autores: Kakulu R, Kemibala E, … Kimaro EG (12 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Zonas fronteiriças de alto fluxo migratório atuam como corredores de introdução e expansão geográfica de Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus e arboviroses.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Levantamento entomológico com armadilhas BG-Pro, CDC light traps, aspiradores Prokopack e inspeção domiciliar de criadouros em áreas transfronteiriças (Mutukula e Namanga), analisado por regressão binomial e de Poisson.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Dos 6.952 mosquitos capturados (84,7% Culex quinquefasciatus, 10,0% Aedes aegypti e 5,3% Anopheles gambiae s.l.), Aedes aegypti e An. funestus s.l. concentraram-se estatisticamente (p < 0,0001) dentro do raio de 400 m da fronteira, incluindo detecção invasiva de Ae. albopictus.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Subsídio epidemiológico espacial para delimitação de zonas tampão entomológicas acima dos 400 m em vigilância de Aedes e Anopheles.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Cruzar índices larvários elevados e pressão antropofílica de borda urbana com perfis de competência vetorial para arbovírus em Ae. aegypti e Ae. albopictus.

43015033.resumo: Arboviral diseases remain a major global public health challenge because mosquito vectors continue to expand their geographical range through increasing international travel, urbanization and climate change. This study aimed to assess the abundance, spatial distribution and larval indices of mosquito vectors of medical importance in a cross-border setting. A comprehensive entomological survey, using multiple collection techniques, was conducted between October and November 2024 at high-traffic cross-border zones at Mutukula ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Uganda and Namanga ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Kenya. Adult mosquitoes were collected using BG-Pro traps, CDC light traps and Prokopack aspirators, while larval surveys were conducted through cross-sectional household inspections of potential breeding habitats. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, and associations between variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Binomial and Poisson regression models were used to identify factors associated with mosquito abundance and breeding site occurrence, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 6952 mosquitoes were collected, comprising Culex quinquefasciatus (84.7%, n = 5895), Aedes aegypti (10.0%, n = 689) and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (5.3%, n = 369). Significantly higher abundance of Aedes spp. and Anopheles funestus s.l was recorded in hamlets located within 400 m of the international border (p < 0.0001), whereas Culex quinquefasciatus predominated in hamlets situated beyond 400 m from the border (χ2 = 1938, p < 0.000001). One female Aedes albopictus was detected among the adult Aedes collections, suggesting the potential introduction of this invasive vector. Four of the 10 hamlets surveyed had larval indices exceeding recommended thresholds, indicating an elevated risk of arboviral transmission. This study revealed a high prevalence of Aedes aegypti within the cross-border buffer zone and a broader distribution of Culex species beyond this zone. These findings underscore the urgent need for sustained vector control interventions and strengthened entomological surveillance and control beyond the International Health Regulations (2005) as amended in 2024, which recommended a 400 m buffer zone at points of entry to mitigate the risk of arboviral disease transmission and potential epidemics.
43015033.metodo: Levantamento entomológico com armadilhas BG-Pro, CDC light traps, aspiradores Prokopack e inspeção domiciliar de criadouros em áreas transfronteiriças (Mutukula e Namanga), analisado por regressão binomial e de Poisson.
43015033.implicacao: Subsídio epidemiológico espacial para delimitação de zonas tampão entomológicas acima dos 400 m em vigilância de Aedes e Anopheles.
43015033.faisca_lateral: 💡 Cruzar índices larvários elevados e pressão antropofílica de borda urbana com perfis de competência vetorial para arbovírus em Ae. aegypti e Ae. albopictus.

43013819.titulo: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination
43013819.autores: Tchouatieu AM, Wells TNC, Achan J (3 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Com 282 milhões de casos e 610 mil óbitos por malária estimados em 2024, urge integrar novas ferramentas profiláticas diante de restrições financeiras e resistência vetorial.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão crítica translacional no NEJM avaliando ensaios clínicos e estratégias de campo para redes impregnadas de nova geração, quimioprevenção sazonal e injetável de longa ação, anticorpos monoclonais e vacinas RTS,S/AS01 e R21/Matrix-M além de intervenções bloqueadoras de transmissão.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Combinações integradas combinando bloqueio pré-eritrocítico (vacinas/mAbs), controle vetorial de nova geração e fármacos bloqueadores de transmissão aceleram a trajetória rumo à eliminação quando ancoradas em vigilância genômica local.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Contextualiza onde alvos experimentais do LUCHM (bloqueio da transmissão no vetor e proteção endotelial na malária grave) se encaixam no pipeline global pós-R21.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Mapear como anticorpos bloqueadores de transmissão interagem com a fisiologia do intestino médio e proteínas peritróficas do vetor.

43013819.resumo: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

43013819.implicacao: Contextualiza onde alvos experimentais do LUCHM (bloqueio da transmissão no vetor e proteção endotelial na malária grave) se encaixam no pipeline global pós-R21.

43015982.titulo: Heterogeneous Permissiveness of Chicken Cells and Tissues to Oropouche Viruses
43015982.autores: Limonta D, Salas-Quinchucua C, … Osorio JE (7 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Surtos massivos do vírus Oropouche (OROV) reemergente na América Latina em 2023–2025 e soropositividade em aves no Brasil levantaram a questão sobre modelos aviários como amplificadores.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Ensaios de permissividade e replicação viral em fibroblastos embrionários de galinha (CEF) e explantes ex vivo de fígado, coração e pulmão desafiados com cepas sul-americanas de OROV, incluindo o novo reassortante circulante.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Fibroblastos e explantes teciduais específicos exibiram permissividade heterogênea e seletiva às cepas sul-americanas e ao reassortante de OROV, estabelecendo um modelo aviário ex vivo reprodutível.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Alinha-se diretamente ao braço de arboviroses emergentes e resposta imune inata antiviral para Oropouche e Culicoides/culicídeos no LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar paralelamente vias de RNAi (Dicer-2/AGO2) e resposta antiviral ao OROV reassortante em células e vetores de laboratório.

43015982.resumo: Massive outbreaks of a reassortant Oropouche virus (OROV) spread across Latin America and the Caribbean in 2023-2025. OROV is a reemerging arbovirus belonging to the trisegmented RNA peribunyavirus family. Viral transmission occurs in sylvatic and urban cycles involving humans and other vertebrates with Culicoides biting midges as the main vector in urban settings. Anti-OROV antibodies have been found in domestic and wild birds in Brazilian OROV-endemic areas. However, no studies exist on the permissiveness of OROV in avian models, and the contribution of birds to the OROV spread remains largely unexplored. Our research indicates that chicken embryonic fibroblasts and chicken tissue explants from the liver, heart, and lung are selectively infected by OROV strains isolated by our group in South America, including the novel OROV reassortant. This work contributes to the development of avian models to investigate new determinants in the infection and transmission of an important arbovirus in the Americas.
43015982.metodo: Ensaios de permissividade e replicação viral em fibroblastos embrionários de galinha (CEF) e explantes ex vivo de fígado, coração e pulmão desafiados com cepas sul-americanas de OROV, incluindo o novo reassortante circulante.
43015982.implicacao: Alinha-se diretamente ao braço de arboviroses emergentes e resposta imune inata antiviral para Oropouche e Culicoides/culicídeos no LUCHM.
43015982.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar paralelamente vias de RNAi (Dicer-2/AGO2) e resposta antiviral ao OROV reassortante em células e vetores de laboratório.

43015069.titulo: The Numb paradox: one protein, multiple isoforms, opposing functions in neurodevelopment, endocytic trafficking, and cancer

resumo_blocos.racional: Numb is a multifunctional adaptor protein that serves as a central regulator of cell fate, linking polarity, signaling, and endocytic trafficking from early development to disease. Initially discovered in Drosophila melanogaster as an intrinsic determinant of asymmetric cell division, Numb's antagonism of Notch signaling has proven to be evolutionarily conserved in mammals, orchestrating the balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation during neurogenesis.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Delineamento experimental descrito no trabalho original (aguardando síntese analítica completa).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Emerging evidence also connects Numb isoform regulation to neurodegenerative processes, including tauopathies and viral neuropathogenesis, as observed in Zika virus infection.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Relevante para a frente de arboviroses emergentes (Oropouche, Dengue, Zika, Mayaro/Chikungunya) e resposta imune/antiviral em vetores e hospedeiros.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar alvos conservados (e.g. macrodomínios virais ou vias de permissividade) frente aos estoques e ensaios de infecção viral do laboratório.

43015069.resumo: Numb is a multifunctional adaptor protein that serves as a central regulator of cell fate, linking polarity, signaling, and endocytic trafficking from early development to disease. Initially discovered in Drosophila melanogaster as an intrinsic determinant of asymmetric cell division, Numb's antagonism of Notch signaling has proven to be evolutionarily conserved in mammals, orchestrating the balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation during neurogenesis. In the mammalian brain, Numb and its paralog, Numb-like (Numbl), integrate polarity cues, receptor trafficking, and transcriptional networks to guide cortical development and maintain neural stem cell homeostasis. Alternative splicing generates multiple Numb isoforms (i.e., p72, p71, p66, and p65) that exhibit distinct structural and functional properties, allowing context-dependent modulation of Notch, p53, and integrin pathways. Isoform-specific expression patterns underlie divergent roles in neurodevelopment, neurite morphogenesis, and tumorigenesis, whereby Numb can act either as a tumor suppressor or as an oncogenic driver. Dysregulated splicing, posttranslational modification, and interaction with RNA-binding proteins such as RBM4, PTBP1, or SRSF9 reprogram Numb's activity across developmental and cancer contexts. 43007987.resumo: Extreme climate events impose significant impacts across the Horn of Africa. One way to monitor these is by using novel digital tools to forecast extreme events and climate-sensitive disease outbreaks. However, limited information exists on stakeholder use of such tools. This qualitative study identified key multidisciplinary stakeholders in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and Uganda, and conducted a needs assessment and gap analysis. Focal persons of multi-lateral agencies, government institutions and ministries, non-governmental organisations, and academic institutions, at regional, national, and sub-national levels, were engaged in Key Informant Interviews (KIIs; N = 63) and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs; N = 7, total participants = 57). Malaria (54.0%), Rift Valley Fever (RVF; 44.4%), cholera (39.7%), dengue fever (27.0%), and anthrax (14.3%) were the most frequently reported climate-sensitive disease priorities amongst KII participants. Country-level variations existed in the use of climate or environmental data to support disease decision-making (Kenya: 95.2% of KII participants, Uganda: 75.0%, Somalia: 64.3%, Ethiopia: 58.3%), electronic reporting systems (Kenya: 42.9%, Ethiopia: 41.7%, Somalia: 14.3%, Uganda: 12.5%), and modelled outputs (Kenya: 57.1%, Uganda: 25.0%, Somalia: 7.1%). FGD participants described barriers to sustainable digitalised systems including cost-effectiveness, lack of technological expertise or support, and poor Internet access, which may be addressed by engaging key national stakeholders, training provision, and financial resources. Overall, digital tool preferences for analysing, displaying or reporting data included provision of data summaries and visual aids, a dashboard format, and functions to download data for further analysis. This study provides critical insights into the needs of disease control stakeholders who would benefit from, and are the likely primary users of, digital tools to tackle the increasing threat of climate-sensitive diseases. It underscores the importance of applying context-specific approaches to supporting local capacity, which will inform the development of a sustainable Climate Sensitive Disease Forecasting Tool (CLIMSEDIS).

43015931.resumo:
Following China's malaria-free certification in 2021, imported malaria infections and the continued presence of Anopheles mosquitoes pose challenges for preventing local transmission in post-elimination settings. We integrated case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data to describe potential conditions for malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China.
We analyzed imported malaria cases reported during 2016-2025, vector surveillance records, and corresponding meteorological data. Five binary indicators-imported case presence, diagnostic delay, Anopheles presence, high Anopheles density, and favorable meteorological conditions-were combined into an exploratory monthly index. Risk scores were tabulated for the 60 months in the May-October surveillance seasons using the available routine surveillance information.
A total of 663 imported malaria cases were reported, of which 611 (92.2%) originated from Africa. In the 37 months with matched vector and meteorological records, concurrent precipitation was positively associated with Anopheles density (Spearman's ρ = 0.360, P = 0.031), whereas mean temperature and dew point temperature 2 months earlier were negatively associated with density (ρ = - 0.504, P = 0.002; and ρ = - 0.578, P < 0.001, respectively). Of the 60 seasonal months, 28 (46.7%) were assigned low-risk scores, 27 (45.0%) moderate-risk scores, and 5 (8.3%) high-risk scores. All five high-risk months occurred in May or June.
The exploratory index identified seasonal variation in the concurrence of routinely monitored indicators, with high-risk scores observed in May and June. Year-round case surveillance and timely diagnosis remain important, alongside vector monitoring during the surveillance season. Uneven monitoring coverage and the lack of validation against local transmission events limit interpretation of the resulting risk categories.

Dengue is endemic in Colombia's Valle del Cauca region. The precise timing and spatial scale of seasonal dengue transmission necessary for effective reactive interventions at the sub-municipal level across the 42 municipalities of Valle del Cauca remain unclear. This study aimed to identify spatio-temporal dengue clusters in Valle del Cauca.
A retrospective observational study was conducted using individual laboratory-confirmed dengue cases, including residential geolocation and consultation dates, reported by healthcare providers to the Sistema Nacional de Vigilancia en Salud Pública (SIVIGILA) in 2022. Residence was utilized as the probable site of infection. Spatio-temporal clustering was analyzed using Kulldorff's space-time scan statistic to identify statistically significant dengue clusters. Results were mapped using R. As a second aim, the association between clinical and demographic characteristics and dengue hospitalization was evaluated. Of 3,964 dengue cases reported in Valle del Cauca in 2022, 2,232 (56%) were laboratory-confirmed. Of these, 1,973 occurred in the defined areas of the nine municipalities included in the spatio-temporal analysis of this study. We identified 28 clusters at the sub-municipal level, with radii of 0-0.98 km, lasting 1-6 months and containing 10-114 cases. Twenty-six clusters (92.9%) spanned both warm-dry and cool-wet seasons, and clusters accounted for 32.0% of spatially analyzed cases. 960 patients were hospitalized. Lower socioeconomic status (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.57), enrollment in the state-subsidized insurance scheme (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.41-2.15) compared with the contributory scheme, and age ≥ 70 years compared to ages 20-29 years (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.51-4.04) were associated with higher odds of hospitalization.
This study identified dengue clusters at the sub-municipal level with the potential to inform reactive dengue control interventions and demonstrated a disproportionate impact on socioeconomically disadvantaged populations and the elderly in Valle del Cauca, Colombia.

43017141.resumo:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are major mosquito-borne arboviruses that increasingly co-circulate in tropical and subtropical regions, including southern China. However, the extent to which these viruses induce shared or distinct host immune responses remains poorly understood. This study aimed to comparatively characterize immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections.
A total of 80 serum samples were analyzed, including 65 samples from patients with laboratory-confirmed DENV-1 (n = 29), DENV-2 (n = 10), or CHIKV (n = 26) infections and 15 healthy controls.Viral RNA was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction. Virus-specific IgM and IgG responses were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and serum cytokines were quantified using a multiplex assay. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests, and associations among antibody responses, cytokine concentrations, and viral RNA levels were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure.
The three infections shared features of interferon-associated immune activation and relatively restrained systemic inflammation but exhibited distinct immune mediator profiles, characterized by differential inflammatory mediator and growth factor responses. After multiple-testing correction, cytokine-cytokine correlation analysis revealed both shared and infection-specific patterns of immune mediator covariation, with shared associations involving IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4, and CXCL1 across all three infection groups. Positive associations between pathogen-specific IgM responses and Ct values were observed across the infections, although the association was not statistically significant for DENV-2 after multiple-testing correction. IgG responses showed a similar association only in DENV-1 infection. Integration of cytokine and antibody profiles further revealed distinct immune association patterns: DENV-1 showed broader associations involving viral RNA levels, inflammatory mediators, and humoral responses, whereas CHIKV displayed a more restricted pattern centered on associations between inflammatory mediators and IgM responses.
These findings reveal shared and distinct immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections and provide a comparative framework for investigating virus-associated immune regulation during acute arboviral infections.

43007258.resumo: Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) are two widespread flaviviruses that pose a significant threat to public health. Owing to their extensive co-circulation and antigenic cross-reactivity, both viruses carry the risk of antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), a phenomenon that renders existing vaccines unable to simultaneously protect against both pathogens. To overcome this limitation, we developed a bispecific mRNA vaccine against ZIKV and DENV (bis-mZDV) by integrating orthogonal B-cell and T-cell modules. The B-cell module was constructed by fusing ZIKV EDIII to the self-adjuvanting complement component C3d to enhance neutralizing antibody titers. The T-cell module incorporated conserved epitopes from ZIKV and DENV, thereby inducing cross-reactive CD8⁺ T cells without eliciting ADE-prone B-cell responses. Notably, the new bis-mZDV achieved up to an 8-fold enhancement in neutralizing antibody titers compared to the unadjuvanted EDIII mRNA vaccine. More importantly, in immunodeficient mice, it conferred protection against both ZIKV and DENV challenges and elicited robust humoral and cellular immune responses. The bis-mZDV represents a promising strategy that may be applicable to co-circulating pathogens and other viruses associated with ADE.

43014495.resumo:
Colombia's tropical climate and low-altitude cities create an ideal environment where mosquito-borne diseases can thrive. During 2013-2014, dengue was the most diagnosed cause of febrile syndrome. However, other viruses like Venezuelan equine encephalitis (VEEV), Mayaro (MAYV), and chikungunya viruses (CHIKV) were also present, and their true prevalence was likely underestimated due to limited surveillance.
We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 90 febrile malaria- and dengue-negative patients from the Urabá region. For each patient, we collected both acute and convalescent serum samples, which were analyzed to detect antibodies against VEEV, CHIKV, and MAYV. Additionally, we attempted virus isolation from the acute-phase serum samples.
We found that antibodies against VEEV were present in 28.3% of samples, CHIKV antibodies were detected in 5%, and MAYV antibodies in 1.7%. Notably, one patient seroconverted against CHIKV even before the first outbreak was recognized in Colombia in 2014. Furthermore, we isolated and fully sequenced VEEV, and our analysis revealed a close phylogenetic relationship with subtype ID Panamanian strains.
This study highlights the need to consider arboviruses beyond just dengue (DENV), when evaluating febrile illness in Colombia. The detection of VEEV and CHIKV, even before they were officially recognized as significant public health threats in this region, underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

43014236.resumo: Viral macrodomains are ADP-ribosylhydrolases encoded within the nonstructural proteins of coronaviruses and alphaviruses-2 RNA virus families with pandemic potential. Genetic studies demonstrate that ADP-ribose binding and ADP-ribosylhydrolase activity are critical for replication in alphaviruses and select coronaviruses, such as Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus and murine hepatitis virus. In contrast, for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and SARS-CoV-2, this domain primarily enhances in vivo fitness by modulating the innate immune response, establishing the macrodomain as a validated antiviral target. Structure-guided and high-throughput efforts have identified selective inhibitors for SARS-CoV-2 and, more recently, early-stage inhibitors of the alphavirus chikungunya virus. Both exploit a conserved active-site architecture that organizes ligand recognition into adenine, phosphate, ribose, and oxyanion subsites. Despite screening of extensive chemical libraries, inhibitor discovery has repeatedly converged on adenine-anchored scaffolds requiring polar engagement of the oxyanion region to achieve potency. This convergence defines a structurally confined druggable corridor but reveals a persistent permeability-potency tradeoff imposed by the polarity required for catalytic engagement. Cross-family comparisons further demonstrate localized divergence that shapes selectivity and constrains straightforward scaffold portability. Here, we synthesize structural, biochemical, and antiviral advances across SARS-CoV-2 and chikungunya virus, define the current boundaries of macrodomain chemical space, and delineate the chemical and biological constraints that now govern translation of catalytic inhibition into predictable antiviral efficacy. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Viral macrodomains have emerged as compelling antiviral targets in 2 pandemic-potential virus families, coronaviruses and alphaviruses, owing to their conservation and role in virulence. This review defines the chemical space and druggability of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and chikungunya virus macrodomains and the structural and biological constraints that must be overcome to translate catalytic inhibition into next-generation antivirals.

43014526.resumo: Aeration strategy-driven utilization of extracellular organic matter was investigated as a key mechanism regulating simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus removal in a mainstream partial nitritation/anammox (PN/A) system. The metabolic pathways through which functional microbial groups utilized organic matter at different C/N ratios depended on the aeration strategy. At high C/N ratios, intermittent aeration promoted aerobic utilization of organic matter, contributing to more rapid suppression of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) and favoring anammox activity. In contrast, at low C/N ratios, Single-stage aeration favored organic matter retention in loosely bound extracellular polymeric substances (LB-EPS), which served as a potential extracellular carbon reservoir. During the anoxic phase, this carbon supported partial denitrification and denitrifying polyphosphate-accumulating organisms, contributing to simultaneous anammox-based nitrogen removal and phosphorus removal. During the aerobic phase, its utilization intensified heterotrophic competition for O2, contributing to NOB suppression. This coordinated utilization supported stable total nitrogen and phosphorus removal efficiencies of 88.5 ± 4.3 % and 73.3 ± 2.4 %, respectively, at a C/N ratio of 2. Microbial community analysis further revealed greater network modularity and more positive associations under Single-stage aeration, whereas intermittent aeration was associated with greater NOB dominance and community variability. Overall, aeration strategy was associated with extracellular carbon utilization by aerobic and anoxic microbial communities, shaping the pathways involved in simultaneous nitrogen and phosphorus removal. These findings provide mechanistic insights into aeration control in mainstream PN/A, extending its role beyond NOB suppression to the regulation of extracellular carbon utilization.

43009002.resumo: Histidine-rich protein 2 (HRP2)-based rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are widely used for the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria in sub-Saharan Africa. However, deletions of the pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 genes threaten the accuracy of these tests by causing false-negative results. This study systematically reviewed and synthesized available evidence on the prevalence of pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 gene deletions and their implications for HRP2-based RDT performance in sub-Saharan Africa. A systematic review and meta-analysis were registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261443503) and were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Four electronic databases were searched for studies published between January 2015 and June 2026. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled prevalence, while heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q, τ², and I² statistics. Twenty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 gene deletions was 3.64% (95% CI: 1.86%-7.01%), 1.63% (95% CI: 0.54%-4.79%), and 1.94% (95% CI: 0.90%-4.14%), respectively. High between-study heterogeneity was observed across all analyses (I² > 91%), reflecting considerable geographical and methodological variability. Diagnostic accuracy analysis demonstrated that HRP2-based RDTs maintained high overall sensitivity and specificity but exhibited reduced sensitivity in settings where pfhrp2 and/or pfhrp3 deletions were prevalent, resulting in false-negative diagnoses and compromised detection of P. falciparum infections. While most studies reported low deletion frequencies, localized hotspots with substantially higher prevalence highlighted areas at greater risk of diagnostic failure. pfhrp2, pfhrp3, and dual gene deletions remain relatively uncommon across sub-Saharan Africa but exhibit marked geographical variation. Their presence can reduce the diagnostic performance of HRP2-based RDTs, underscoring the need for continuous molecular surveillance, routine monitoring of RDT performance, and the adoption of complementary diagnostic strategies in areas with increasing deletion prevalence.

43014996.resumo: Rice agroecosystems are among the most productive mosquito habitats in Asia, but the ways in which crop phenology and urbanisation-driven environmental changes shape immature mosquito vector populations remain poorly understood. We quantified mosquito larvae and pupae dynamics across two crop seasons in a rice field located in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam, using generalised linear models with appropriate error distributions. A total of 3196 immature mosquitoes representing six species were collected. Overall mosquito abundance was significantly higher in spring than in autumn and peaked during the vegetative stage. Species richness did not vary between seasons but declined significantly at later crop stages. Larval-stage structure varied with both season and crop phenology. Early instars were more prevalent in spring and during the reproductive stage, whereas late instars dominated in autumn and declined during the ripening stage. The proportion of pupae decreased during the reproductive stage. Among dominant taxa, Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Anopheles barbirostris showed strong seasonal responses, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus exhibited no significant temporal variation. Environmental drivers differed among species. Culex tritaeniorhynchus was positively associated with water depth, pH and dissolved oxygen, but negatively associated with conductivity. In contrast, Cx. quinquefasciatus was strongly associated with higher conductivity, while An. barbirostris showed negative associations with temperature and conductivity. These findings indicate that mosquito development in rice fields is jointly structured by crop seasonality and agronomic water management, with early crop stages creating favourable conditions for larval proliferation. The dominance of vector species of epidemiological concern underscores the need to integrate phenology-based habitat management into nuisance and mosquito vector control strategies in Hanoi and similar peri-urban rice-growing landscapes.

43005892.resumo: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) develops through interactions between hepatocyte injury and hepatic immune responses. Lipid droplets (LDs) exposed or released from damaged hepatocytes provide a potential link between lipid accumulation and macrophage-mediated inflammation. Experimental studies indicate that these structures can both promote disease-associated macrophage responses and attenuate inflammatory signaling. This mini-review examines how hepatocyte-derived LDs influence macrophage sensing, uptake, and inflammatory responses in MASH. We discuss the contribution of membrane-spanning 4-domains A7 (MS4A7) to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and disease progression, alongside evidence that LD treatment suppresses inflammatory responses in cultured macrophages. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) supports this suppression without being required for LD uptake in the tested system, while reduced MS4A7 expression contributes to the attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings distinguish LD internalization from its downstream immune effects and warrant separate consideration from the efferocytosis of intact apoptotic hepatocytes. We examine experimental conditions and macrophage states as possible explanations for differing outcomes and identify unresolved questions about LD recognition and relevance to human disease. Finally, we consider therapeutic strategies that limit pathogenic macrophage activation while preserving beneficial clearance functions. Defining the molecular basis of LD sensing and establishing its consequences in vivo will be essential for translating this form of hepatocyte-macrophage communication into immunological interventions for MASH.

43015102.resumo: While the nervous system is organized by two main types of connections between neurons, electrical and chemical synapses, most studies focus upon the contribution of the molecularly complex and functionally diverse chemical synapse. Electrical synapses, in contrast, are perceived as simple, neuronal gap junction channels between contacts, often thought to be replaced in early development by more sophisticated chemical synapses. However, recent work and new tools push for the redefining of electrical synapse molecular architecture and function to allow for an updated interpretation of their ongoing contributions to neural circuit formation and function. Here, we describe fresh insight into neuronal gap junction structure, function, and molecular composition within invertebrate (nematodes, drosophila) and vertebrate (zebrafish, rabbit, rodent) model organisms across a variety of time periods and brain regions. Through molecular, genetic, connectomic, and functional explorations, our results argue for a new appreciation of electrical synapse heterogeneity. Based on these and other points of emerging new evidence, we argue for increased consideration of electrical synapses as complex and diverse structures which interact with chemical synapses to drive circuit formation and function.

10.64898/2026.05.30.728996.titulo: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
10.64898/2026.05.30.728996.autores: Vijayakumar P, Cauwenberghs K, … Su C-Y (7 autores)

resumo_blocos.racional: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. 43005096.resumo: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) provides the sole source of NADPH in mature erythrocytes, fueling the cell's essential antioxidant defenses. Limitations include the gap between mechanistic and clinical evidence, uncertainty regarding the relevance of proposed mechanisms, the context-dependent nature of metformin signaling, and the inherent limitations of observational studies. Overall, metformin is a biologically plausible therapeutic candidate for CLD, but its future clinical role will depend on integrating mechanistic insights with rigorous translational and clinical research to identify patients most likely to benefit.

43009706.resumo:
From 2024-2026, hospitals were mandated by Centers for Medicare and Medicaid (CMS) to screen for five health-related social needs (HRSN); however, patients experience additional HRSN that affect their health. Understanding all HRSN experienced among patients in large health systems is important to improve health.
To describe rates of patient-reported HRSN across 5 CMS-mandated, and 8 additional domains.
We conducted a cross-sectional study of all patient HRSN screenings completed in a large health system from July 2021 to June 2023. We summarized overall HRSN rates and utilized generalized estimating equation models to determine odds of experiencing HRSN across demographics.
Patients from a large, Midwestern healthcare system, aged ≥ 18 years and residing in the USA (n = 559,118).
Associations between patient demographics (sex assigned at birth, race, ethnicity, age, health insurance) and HRSN reported in 13 domains-five required by CMS (domestic violence; food, housing, and transportation insecurity; utility affordability) and eight additional domains (barriers due to physical/mental health; dependent care; employment; education; healthcare affordability; literacy; legal issues; social connections).
Four non-CMS-mandated categories had higher prevalence than any CMS-mandated category (barriers due to physical/mental health, 23.6%; education, 11.4%; social connections, 10.4%; literacy, 5.3%). Black patients and patients of Other race, patients aged 18-29 and 50-64 years old, and patients with Medicare/Medicare Supplement, Dual Medicaid + Medicare, Self-pay, and Other insurance had higher odds of reporting all CMS-required HRSN. Relative odds of other HRSN varied based on demographic characteristics.
This is one of the first studies to compare CMS-mandated HRSN and additional HRSN domains from a population-wide screening program. Future research should investigate what drives reported HRSN prevalence differences and ensure successful HRSN screening and intervention implementation across population subgroups. Determining which HRSN domains should be mandated by entities like CMS is paramount to addressing patient needs impacting health.

43013753.resumo: Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) are key to sustainable hydrogen production, but their long-term performance is limited by degradation, particularly in the membrane electrode assembly (MEA), which remains a barrier to commercial viability. Moreover, the need for corrosion-resistant materials and the intricate fabrication of bipolar plates and porous transport layers (PTLs) further impede large-scale deployment and account for a major share of the stack cost. Because lifetime and replacement costs are strongly influenced by the local microstructure and contact conditions, especially at the anode/PTL interface, a multiscale characterization approach combining 3D focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) with time-of-flight mass spectrometry is used to investigate degradation in an MEA after several thousand hours of operation under industrially relevant conditions. The 3D reconstruction and ppm-level chemical mapping show that local contact heterogeneities at welds in an expanded-metal mesh PTL act as degradation hotspots. At these sites, intensified catalyst utilization accelerates iridium dissolution, driving iridium migration and deposition as extended filaments into the membrane. Concurrently, membrane voids are formed beneath these sites, accompanied by iron contamination detected at both contact types. In contrast, general contact regions mainly show a thin redeposition layer without voids or filaments. These findings provide a mechanistic framework that links local contact conditions and microstructural heterogeneities to coupled catalyst and membrane degradation, supporting design rules for improved PEMWE durability.

43014937.resumo: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) threaten freshwater ecosystems and are linked to nutrient cycling. We conducted a metagenomic investigation in China's Yuqiao Reservoir, which experiences filamentous cyanobacterial blooms (Pseudanabaena and Cylindrospermopsis), to elucidate microbial mechanisms driving nitrogen and phosphorus cycling during HABs. 28 genes for both nitrogen-cycling and phosphorus-cycling showed significantly different abundances between bloom and non-bloom periods. Bloom periods exhibited unified, energy-efficient metabolic strategies, featuring upregulated genes for nitrogen uptake via ammonia assimilation (gltB/D) and enhanced inorganic phosphorus uptake, including high-affinity phosphate transporters (pstA/B/C) and polyphosphate storage genes (ppk1, phoU), supporting rapid microbial proliferation. Conversely, non-bloom periods showed a metabolic transition to diversified nitrogen acquisition, including upregulation of nitrate assimilation, nitrification, denitrification, coupled nitrification-denitrification, and nitrogen fixation. Organic phosphorus mineralization genes became predominant. Concurrently, significant restructuring occurred in both nitrogen- and phosphorus-cycling communities. Although composed predominantly of Actinobacteria, Cyanobacteria, and Proteobacteria in both periods, keystone taxon analysis revealed a critical functional shift from an "autotrophic cyanobacteria-driven" pattern during blooms to a "heterotrophic bacteria-mediated metabolism" in non-bloom phases. Microbial co-occurrence network analysis indicated that the algal bloom triggered a fundamental community reorganization, from a broadly cooperative and stable structure to a more partitioned and potentially specialized state, reflecting strong niche partitioning due to altered environmental conditions. Partial least squares path modeling confirmed that algal blooms govern functional gene abundance by driving microbial community restructuring. Our findings demonstrate that microbial metabolic pattern mediated by algal blooms determined the unification of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling genes, revealing the mechanisms of HABs' ecological impacts.

In this study, Siamese banana peel (SBP) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for the synthesis of AgNPs. The effects of reaction time, AgNO3 solution concentration, and the volume ratio between the AgNO3 solution and banana peel extract on the formation of AgNPs were evaluated using UV-Vis spectroscopy via surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The physicochemical characteristics of AgNPs under optimal conditions were assessed via UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, and HR-TEM analyses. Antibacterial activity was evaluated by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) against nine microbial strains, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The results showed that the suitable synthesis conditions included a reaction time of 120 minutes, an AgNO3 concentration of 2.0 mM, and an AgNO3 solution-to-extract volume ratio of 30 : 20 (v/v). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis revealed that the nanoparticles were predominantly spherical, well-dispersed, with sizes ranging within 28.3 ± 10.1 nm. XRD and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) analyses indicated that the AgNPs possessed a face-centered cubic (fcc) crystalline structure of metallic silver, whereas FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of phytochemical functional groups involved in nanoparticle formation and surface stabilization. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited antibacterial activity across all tested strains, with MIC/MBC ratios ranging from 2 to 4, demonstrating significant bactericidal efficacy under the experimental conditions.

43005992.resumo: Micronutrient deficiencies, particularly those involving zinc (Zn), iron (Fe), selenium (Se), and iodine (I), remain major constraints to human nutrition and food security. Crop biofortification offers a sustainable approach to increasing the concentration and bioavailability of these elements in staple foods. Still, its effectiveness depends on the processes regulating their behavior across the soil-plantsoil-plant continuum. This structured narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the edaphic, rhizospheric, physiological, and molecular mechanisms controlling Zn, Fe, Se, and I mobility, acquisition, transport, redistribution, storage, and accumulation in edible plant organs. Literature searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar, focusing primarily on studies published between 2021 and 18 March 2026, while retaining foundational research required to explain key mechanisms. The evidence indicates that parent material, texture, cation exchange capacity, pH, redox potential, organic matter, and nutrient interactions govern micronutrient speciation and availability. Plants respond through rhizosphere acidification, chelator and organic acid release, microbial associations, and coordinated transporter networks. Zinc and Fe homeostasis involves ZIP/IRT, HMA, YSL, NRAMP, MTP, VIT, and related transport systems. In contrast, Se largely shares sulfate and phosphate pathways, and iodine appears to use anion transport systems associated with chloride. Agronomic fertilization can rapidly increase micronutrient concentrations, while breeding, biotechnology, and gene editing can improve uptake, remobilization, and storage. The most promising strategies integrate soil diagnosis, appropriate nutrient sources and application methods, genotype selection, microbial processes, bioavailability, and food-system considerations. Such integration is essential for producing nutritionally improved crops without compromising yield, environmental sustainability, or consumer acceptance.

artigo_base.resumo_analitico: Revisão seminal de Michael Levin na Cell demonstrando como padrões bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem) e correntes iônicas funcionam como circuitos de software que orquestram a identidade celular, adesão tecidual e barreiras epiteliais, operando ordens de magnitude mais rápido que a reprogramação transcricional clássica.

ensaio.historia:
Durante quase um século, a parasitologia molecular operou sob um dogma redutor: para entender por que um mosquito transmite ou bloqueia a malária, ou por que o camundongo desenvolve edema cerebral, deveríamos buscar sempre "o gene" ou "a citocina". Mapeamos vias inteiras (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT), sequenciamos transcriptomas de células únicas e quantificamos centenas de RNAs mensageiros.

No entanto, uma pergunta desconfortável permaneceu sem resposta na bancada: **como decisões vitais de infecção ocorrem em frações de segundo, muito antes de qualquer RNA polimerase conseguir transcrever um gene?**

Quando o oocineto atinge o microvilo do mosquito, a digestão do sangue está no auge. Milhões de eritrócitos se rompem, gerando uma pressão coloidosmótica massiva, liberação letal de hemo livre e fluxo turbulento não-newtoniano. O parasito não tem horas para esperar uma via gênica ser ativada. Ele precisa explorar as propriedades biofísicas nativas do epitélio: diferenças de potencial elétrico entre células vizinhas, zonas de menor tensão mecânica e condensação líquida de proteínas de superfície.

Se quisermos descobrir o que não sabemos que existe, precisamos sair da nossa própria vizinhança conceitual. É no cruzamento com a biologia de sistemas de organelas, com a bioeletricidade do desenvolvimento e com a física da matéria mole que residem as próximas grandes viradas da nossa bancada.

grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Contactoma Celular & Comunicação Não-Vesicular de Organelas
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Maya Schuldiner revolucionou a biologia celular ao quebrar o paradigma de que as organelas intracelulares se comunicavam exclusivamente através de vesículas secretoras (via clássica de Golgi e retículo).

Usando triagem robótica em larga escala de leveduras (SGA - Synthetic Genetic Array) combinada com microscopia de fluorescência de altíssima resolução, seu laboratório no Weizmann descobriu que organelas como retículo endoplasmático, mitocôndrias, peroxissomos, gotas lipídicas e vacúolos estão fisicamente conectadas por pontes proteicas especializadas ("tethers"), formando uma malha contínua chamada de 'contactoma'. Essas fendas de 10 a 30 nanômetros permitem o transporte ultrarrápido de lipídios, íons cálcio e intermediários metabólicos vitais, operando como cabos de alta velocidade dentro da célula.

grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Michael Levin é pioneiro na redefinição da biologia do desenvolvimento e regeneração: enquanto a maioria dos biólogos encara eletricidade celular como algo restrito a neurônios e músculos, Levin provou que **todas as células vivas mantêm gradientes bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem)** e se comunicam através de junções comunicantes (gap junctions).

Seu grupo demonstrou que redes bioelétricas funcionam como um 'software de alto nível' que define a morfologia anatômica, a regeneração de membros e o comportamento inflamatório, conseguindo induzir o crescimento de olhos funcionais em caudas de girinos ou reprogramar tecidos apenas alterando a condutância iônica local.

temas_expansao.o_que_e: Como os sítios de contato membrana-membrana desviam a toxicidade do hemo livre no intestino de mosquitos hematófagos durante o repasto sanguíneo.
temas_expansao.pergunta_provocativa: Como os sítios de contato membrana-membrana desviam a toxicidade do hemo livre no intestino de mosquitos hematófagos?
temas_expansao.contexto:
Durante a digestão da hemoglobina, a concentração de hemo livre no intestino médio atinge níveis milimolares letais. Sabíamos que os mosquitos contam com agregação de hemo em hemozoína e proteção por antioxidantes.

temas_expansao.contexto:

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectroscopia AFM-IR em Nanoescala (Photo-Thermal Induced Resonance)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Combinação de Microscopia de Força Atômica com Espectroscopia de Infravermelho (AFM-IR), permitindo caracterização química de espécies moleculares com resolução espacial de 10 a 20 nanômetros.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Durante décadas, a espectroscopia de infravermelho clássica (FTIR) foi limitada pelo limite de difração da luz óptica (~2 a 10 micrômetros), sendo incapaz de identificar compostos químicos dentro de organelas isoladas.

O desenvolvimento do AFM-IR contornou esse limite físico ao utilizar a ponta ultrafina de um microscópio de força atômica para detectar a expansão térmica nanomecânica da amostra quando excitada por um laser infravermelho pulsado e sintonizável. Com isso, tornou-se possível obter o espectro de absorção química exato de nanodomínios lipídicos, agregados amiloides e depósitos minerais sem marcadores fluorescentes.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Optogenética Não-Invasiva em Insetos Vivos (Canais CsChrimson)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Controle óptico remoto de neurônios, enterócitos e células musculares em mosquitos livres e intactos, usando luz vermelha profunda (CsChrimson) que penetra a cutícula sem lesão térmica.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Por décadas, testar a função de um circuito neuropeptídico ou da motilidade intestinal de um mosquito exigia dissecção traumática, microinjeção de drogas ou silenciamento por RNAi sistêmico (que afeta o inseto por dias).

A criação de canais de rodopsina de canal ativados por luz vermelha (CsChrimson, desenvolvidos por Boyden, Levin e colaboradores) permitiu que pesquisadores ativem subpopulações neurais e células enteroendócrinas específicas com um simples flash de LED vermelho enquanto o inseto voa ou se alimenta em tempo real, sem qualquer agulha ou anestesia.
